The FOMC statement leans modestly hawkish on strong Q3 growth and still-elevated inflation while maintaining rates and ongoing QT. However, the latest Beige Book reports broadly softer momentum: many districts noted flat-to-slower consumer spending, easing labor-market tightness and wage pressures, slower but still positive price increases, and tighter credit with weaker loan demand. CRE—especially office—remains under pressure, and real estate contacts in New York remain pessimistic, though tourism activity is mixed-to-solid in some districts. These anecdotes reinforce that tighter financial and credit conditions are weighing on activity and inflation, tilting the overall policy tone toward a cautious hold rather than further near-term firming.
